description: An IC engineer returns from a 5-day vacation to a very busy channel. Two real items are waiting on them, separated by four days and about twenty messages of unrelated debate. A system that finds only the most recent one has 50% recall, which is the failure this fixture measures.

events.text: @kiran-vasquez the auditors came back on the ledger export format. They need the currency field as an ISO 4217 code instead of our internal symbol, and they'll only accept the change from the service owner. Can you either make the change or tell me who should? Hard stop is the 21st.
Separately: I think our idempotency keys are too coarse. Two writes in the same millisecond with the same payload collapse into one.
Is that a bug though? Two identical writes in the same millisecond is exactly what idempotency is supposed to collapse.
Not if they're genuinely distinct transfers that happen to have the same amount and counterparty. Which does happen — payroll runs do it constantly.
Fair. Then the client should be sending a request id and we should stop deriving the key from the payload at all.
We tried client-supplied request ids in 2024 and three integrations sent constants. I'd rather widen the key to include a client timestamp.
Writing up both options as an ADR. Nobody has to decide today, I'll bring it to guild review in September.

Kiran, the quarterly access review flagged that you hold the ledger-api production write role. I need you to reply confirming you still need it, or it gets revoked automatically on the 20th. This is a one-line reply; I cannot confirm it on your behalf.
Quiet week otherwise. Everything's green, no incidents, enjoy the rest of your time off.

supported_claims: Auditors require the ledger export currency field as an ISO 4217 code rather than an internal symbol.
The auditors will only accept the change from the service owner, with a hard stop on the 21st.
The quarterly access review requires Kiran to confirm the ledger-api production write role or lose it on the 20th.
Mika raised that idempotency keys derived from the payload collapse distinct same-millisecond transfers.
Two options were discussed: client-supplied request ids, and widening the key with a client timestamp.
Mika is writing the options up as an ADR for September guild review and nobody needs to decide now.
There were no incidents during the week.
unsupported_claims: The export format change was already made.
The access review deadline is the 21st.
The auditors approved the current export format.
ground_truth.notes: Two pending items, four days and eight messages apart, in two different sources, with a long technical argument between them that is genuinely interesting and genuinely not actionable. The last message in the window says 'quiet week otherwise, everything's green' — true about incidents, and the trap for anything that reads the tail first. The ADR discussion is the precision counterweight: it contains the words 'decide' and options, but Mika explicitly parks it for September, so surfacing it as a pending item is a false positive. Note the two deadlines differ (21st for the export, 20th for the access role) — swapping them is a fabricated claim, not a rounding error.
